statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 10% sits in the low band, well below the 25% block threshold, while Stress 46% reflects a genuinely difficult yield and inflation backdrop.
recommendation: Tail remains below the watch threshold, so the mapped state is EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The published danger window is narrow and covers the 06 October US cash open, where continuation from a record close is the main conditional checkpoint. Elevated Stress alongside low Tail describes a volatile but still mean-reverting environment.
headline: NQ Globex holds a 60-point range after a record NDX close at 31,076.44; Tail low, Stress elevated with the 10-year at 5.31%.
body: The NDX cash session closed at a record 31,076.44, up 268.51 points (+0.87%) from a 30,807.93 previous close, with a 30,798.42-31,117.36 range that opened near the low and finished in the upper third; the session high matched the 52-week high. Nvidia set an all-time high near $238 and Taiwan Semiconductor touched an intraday record, with megacap technology and semiconductors leading. Since the 22:00 UTC Globex reopen, NQ futures have held a 31,325.50-31,385.25 range and trade at 31,347.50 (+0.09%), roughly a third off the session low rather than at an extreme, and the live Asian handover is orderly with the ASX 200 up 0.4% at 8,723 on 152 advancers to 40 decliners. The advance occurred against bond weakness rather than with it: the 10-year rose 3bp to 5.31% within a 5.26-5.35 range and close to its highest since 2002, while H.15 shows the 2-year at 4.83% and the 30-year at 5.63%. VIX closed at 15.52 in a 15.48-16.38 range. WTI fell 1.84% to $89.18 and Brent 1.89% to $100.23 after Saudi Aramco cut its November Arab Light price to Asian buyers to $5 below the regional benchmark. September ISM Services came in at 54.9 against a 55.0 consensus with its prices component at 74.0, while the final S&P Global Services PMI was 58.8. September payrolls of 29,000 and a 4.2% unemployment rate have cut October rate-hike pricing to roughly 17% ahead of the 27-28 October FOMC. The result is a directional cash uptrend without confirming cross-asset alignment and a contained overnight range, which the contract treats as a Stress and conviction question rather than evidence of mean-reversion failure, so Tail stays in the low band. The shared Finviz context file is six days stale and marked partial, so it was not used; this assessment rests on independent current research.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 published hours open in the mid-teens through the Asian session, decay to a 6% Tail low at 08:00 UTC, then rebuild through the US cash session as megacap leadership firmed. The 19:00 UTC hour reached Tail 20% and the WATCH state during the late-session advance before easing to 17%, 14% and 11% after the cash close. Stress fell steadily from 65% to a 46% trough around midday and then rebuilt into the low fifties before easing again. Dominant mode rotated between normal, mixed and trend-up, with a single trend-down print at 10:00 UTC. The 06:00 UTC slot has no published assessment and stays explicitly unavailable.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours cover the Asian session, the European cash session and the 06 October US cash session. Conditional Tail sits at a 9% floor through the thinnest overnight and maintenance-break hours, rises through the European open into the low teens, and peaks at 20% and the WATCH state for the 13:00 UTC hour containing the US cash open and the 14:45 UTC Bowman speech, where continuation from a record close is the main conditional checkpoint. It then decays through the US afternoon, firms modestly into the 20:00 UTC cash close, and returns to the floor during the 21:00 UTC CME maintenance break. No forecast hour reaches the 25% block threshold. Stress stays in the elevated band for all but the quietest overnight hours on an unchanged 5.31% 10-year, Brent above $100 and a services prices component at 74.0. Scheduled checkpoints beyond this horizon are the 07 October FOMC minutes, the 08 October jobless claims and 30-year auction, and the 27-28 October FOMC meeting.
